messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we still don't have a clear contract for route precedence when a customer advertises an on-prem route that overlaps our regional relay route. need deterministic tie-breaker so failovers aren't flappy.
anjali: Agree. Without a rule we see oscillation during peering rebuilds. Two quick options: prefer customer-provided route (stick to tenant), or prefer our relay route (stick to platform).
kevin: What's the explicit failure surface for preferring customer routes? if their on-prem BGP goes noisy we could blackhole traffic for a tenant until they fix it.
maria: Right — preferring customer route reduces NAT/cost churn (preserves source IP), but increases blast radius if their route is bad. Preferring relay reduces blast radius but may change srcip and increase NAT cost.
zane: Can we have a hybrid: prefer customer route only when it meets health criteria (stable for X seconds / AS-PATH length / no withdraws)? otherwise fallback to relay.
maria: I like the health-gated approach. Propose metrics: 60s consecutive announcements, no >1 withdraw in last 5m, and AS-PATH length within 2 of previous stableness.
anke: ops-bot: annotate — we need observability hooks to alert when we switch precedence per-tenant.
ops-bot: noted — will emit tenant.route_precedence.change events with reason tag (health, config, manual).
kevin: Implementation idea: attach a route "score" at route ingestion: base score customer=100, relay=90. apply penalties for withdraws/instability (-50), longer AS-PATHs (-10 per hop beyond threshold), flapping penalty (-30 if >2 withdraws in 5m). choose highest score.
anjali: +1 to scoring model. Also add manual override tag for enterprise customers who require strict stickiness to their route.
zane: Edge case: simultaneous peering fail and on-prem flapping -> both routes unstable. Need default deterministic tie-breaker, e.g., lower origin preference wins, then path length, then lexicographic of next-hop ip to avoid nondeterminism.
maria: Documenting decision: scoring model as kevin suggested, with thresholds Maria proposed. Manual override available. Tie-breaker deterministic fallback: origin-pref -> shorter AS-PATH -> next-hop ip.
anjali: Can we get a short runbook? e.g., how to debug when tenant complains about sudden srcip change. Steps: check tenant.route_precedence.change events -> route score history -> peering health dashboard -> recommend giving manual override or adjust timers.
maria: I'll draft the runbook after we land thresholds. Quick ask: objections to the scoring + health-gate approach?
kevin: no objections from infra side. We'll need a little extra headroom on route evaluation CPU but fine.
zane: Ops and SRE OK?
anjali: SRE here — fine, add an alert if score flips >3 times in 10m.
maria: Great. I'll open a follow-up RFC PR with numeric thresholds and runbook. tagging @kevin @anjali for review. :thumbsup:
